outcome: No proof of the Marcus-de Oliveira determinantal conjecture for general n has been found dated since 26 January 2024. The window holds a 2024 Auburn PhD dissertation (Speck, advisor Oeding) whose abstract describes a reduction and does not claim a proof, a 2025 Izvestiya paper (Shitov) that proves containment only when all eigenvalues of A are real and all but three eigenvalues of B are real, a 2025 MDPI survey that calls the problem open, and a 2026 LAA paper (Mulero-Martinez) whose abstract I could not read. A January 2023 talk abstract by Oeding (joint with Speck) claimed a complete proof, but that predates the window and no written argument for it has been found. No AI system is named in any source found for this conjecture.
problem_asks: One conjecture, quantified over every n >= 1 and every pair of n-by-n normal complex matrices A and B with eigenvalues a_1..a_n and b_1..b_n. The claim: det(A+B) lies in the convex hull of the n! complex numbers prod_i (a_i + b_{sigma(i)}), with sigma ranging over the permutations of {1..n}. Wikipedia's wording (per its lead, as fetched) is the determinant of A+B lies in the convex hull of the n! points. Parts: (a) containment of det(A+B) in that convex hull, for all n, for all normal A and B. That is the only part the bullet names. The literature usually writes A-B (equivalent after replacing B by -B). The bullet says nothing about the shape of the region, about equality cases, or about any restricted class; those are not parts of the problem as stated.

events.what_happened: Fiedler, 'Bounds for the determinant of the sum of Hermitian matrices', Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1971). Cited as reference 11 in Shitov's 2025 paper (reference list read via the journal page). Described as the motivating result: for Hermitian A and B, the set of determinants det(A+UBU*) over unitary U is a line segment whose endpoints are sigma-points. That description comes from search-result summaries of Bebiano-da Providencia and Rodtes, not from the original paper, which I did not open.
events.delivers: Restricted to Hermitian pairs (all eigenvalues real), and to the one-parameter family det(A+UBU*). Its values lie on a segment with sigma-points at the ends, so they lie in the convex hull of the sigma-points. Establishes the containment for Hermitian A and B only.
events.remains: Every pair of normal matrices that is not Hermitian (non-real eigenvalues on either side), so the containment for general normal A and B.

events.what_happened: Kovacec, 'The Marcus-de Oliveira conjecture, bilinear forms, and cones', Linear Algebra Appl. 289 (1999) 243-259. The abstract was read only through a search-result copy of the Coimbra repository record; the record page itself did not open. Per that abstract: the n=4 subcase with X Hermitian and Y normal is recast as a statement about a family of bilinear forms on R^16 x C^16; the method succeeds for a unitary similarity from Drury's work; the natural extension of the bilinear assertion to complex arguments is false; the n=4 case is reformulated as a question about cones, which would follow from showing certain semialgebraic sets are empty; and computer experiments are reported. The abstract says the n=4 subcase is still open. Shitov's introduction, as quoted in a search-result snippet, credits this paper with the case of one non-real eigenvalue of B.
events.delivers: Per its abstract: no established case of the containment for general n. The paper states the n=4 subcase with X Hermitian and Y normal is still open. Per Shitov's introduction (snippet only), it settles the case where all eigenvalues are real except possibly one eigenvalue of B.
events.remains: The n=4 subcase with X Hermitian and Y normal (per the abstract), and general n. The variant with complex arguments is false, which is a different statement from the conjecture.

events.direction: Partial: supports the conjecture for one non-real eigenvalue (per Shitov's introduction, snippet only). Its own abstract leaves the n=4 subcase open and reports a false variant.

events.what_happened: Talk by Luke Oeding, 'Determinants of Sums of Normal Matrices', 'joint work with Matt Speck', Georgia Tech algebra seminar, Monday 30 January 2023 (page opened). Abstract: the determinantal range of the sum of two normal matrices with prescribed eigenvalues is a flattened solid twisted permutahedron, a finite union of flattened solid twisted hypercubes with prescribed vertices. It states: 'This complete geometric description, in particular, proves the conjecture.' A companion Auburn seminar listing (2023/01, same title) appeared in search results but did not open. No written argument has been found for this claim.
events.delivers: As stated in the abstract: the containment for all n, via a geometric description of the determinantal range. The argument is not in any source I could read.
events.remains: Per the abstract, nothing. But no written argument was found, and the same authors' later Auburn material describes a reduction (2024 dissertation) or n=3 progress (2024 talk).
events.doubts: The claim exists only as a talk abstract. An arXiv author search for Oeding (34 entries, 2008-2026) and for Speck (0 entries) found no normal-matrix paper by either. The 2024 talk and 2024 dissertation describe the same project as n=3 progress or as a reduction, so the scope claimed in January 2023 does not appear in any later written statement I could read. Under the first-written-argument rule, a talk is dated to its write-up; no write-up was found, so the date rests on the abstract.
events.direction: Claims to prove the conjecture in full, which would cut in its favour, for all n.
events.object: A geometric description, not an explicit object: the determinantal range of det(A+B) over normal A, B with prescribed spectra is claimed to be a flattened solid twisted permutahedron, a finite union of flattened solid twisted hypercubes with prescribed vertices. The abstract gives no formula, vertex list or check.

events.what_happened: Matthew Speck, 'Determinants of Sums of Normal Matrices', PhD dissertation, Auburn University, Mathematics and Statistics, issued 2024-05-06, advisor Luke Oeding (the only advisor listed; no other committee members on the record). The ETD metadata was opened. Abstract (paraphrased from the record): it addresses a conjecture on the determinant of the sum of two normal matrices; it reduces the conjecture to finding non-negative solutions of a rank-deficient linear system; it uses representation theory and combinatorics to describe the modifications such solutions need; and it proposes a statistical approach to the broader problem. It does not state that the conjecture is proved. The embargo field reads EMBARGO_GLOBAL, 12 months, end date 2025-05-06, status EMBARGOED. The PDF ('Speck Dissertation Final.pdf', 2.52 MB) came back as binary that my tools could not decode, so its text was not read.
events.delivers: Per the abstract only: a reduction of the conjecture to a non-negativity question for a rank-deficient linear system, a description of the modifications needed, and a statistical approach. Whether the text proves any case is unknown to me.
events.remains: Per the abstract, the conjecture as a whole. The abstract makes no claim to settle it.
events.doubts: Two points. (1) The 2023 talk by the same author team claims a complete proof, but this dissertation's abstract describes a reduction, so the scope appears to have narrowed between the two; the body would show which, and I could not read it. (2) The only listed advisor is Oeding, who gave the 2023 talk, so the dissertation is not an independent reading of that claim. The embargo end date (2025-05-06) has passed, but the record still showed EMBARGOED when I read it, so current access is unknown.
events.direction: Unknown from the abstract. It frames the work as a reduction and does not say whether it cuts for or against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Yaroslav N. Shitov, 'A further sufficient condition for the determinantal conjecture', Izvestiya: Mathematics 89:4 (2025), pp. 862-869 (Russian original Izv. RAN Ser. Mat. 89:4 (2025), 219-226; DOI 10.4213/im9292). The journal's Russian page was opened and gives volume, issue, pages and DOI. Abstract (paraphrased from that page, which exceeded my quoting limit): for n-by-n normal A and B with eigenvalues (a_i) and (b_i), det(A+B) lies in the convex hull of the products prod(a_i + b_{psi(i)}) over permutations psi, provided all eigenvalues of A and B are real except three eigenvalues of B. The received date (21 Nov 2021) and the 2025 publication dates (August 2025; two different days) come from search-result snippets, not the page, and conflict. No arXiv or other preprint was found, so the journal publication is the first public written argument I can find.
events.delivers: The containment, under the hypothesis that all eigenvalues of A are real and all but at most three eigenvalues of B are real. Restricted to normal A with real spectrum and B with at most three non-real eigenvalues. Per a search summary of the paper, it improves the one-non-real-eigenvalue case of Kovacec 1999 and the all-real case of Fiedler.
events.remains: Normal pairs where A has any non-real eigenvalue, and normal pairs where B has four or more non-real eigenvalues (for n >= 4).

disputes.summary: The January 2023 Oeding talk abstract (joint with Speck) says the geometric description 'proves the conjecture' in full. The January 2024 Speck talk, per a search summary, claims a novel proof for n=3 only. The May 2024 dissertation abstract describes a reduction and does not claim a proof. The record does not show which of these the authors stand behind, and the dissertation body is unread.

The publication year of Marcus's paper is given as 1972 in Wikipedia's article and as 1973 in Bebiano-da Providencia's abstract. Rodtes cites it as Indiana Univ. Math. J. 22 (1972/73), per a search summary. The date of the conjecture is not an event; it is recorded here only because the two sources differ.

summary: Sources checked: the Wikipedia article (a stub; it names Marcus 1972 and de Oliveira 1982), the Georgia Tech seminar record for the 2023 Oeding talk, the Auburn ETD records for Speck's 2024 dissertation and Homadi's 2017 thesis (metadata only, because the PDFs returned binary), Drury's ELA abstracts (2004 and 2006), Shitov's 2025 Izvestiya paper (journal page), the Bebiano-da Providencia 2025 MDPI survey (abstract only, via RePEc, because MDPI blocked the fetch), the Mulero-Martinez 2026 LAA record (metadata only), Rodtes's arXiv abstract (2020), Sharma's viXra abstract (2018), and arXiv author and title searches. The main question is the Speck-Oeding claim. A January 2023 talk abstract says a complete geometric description proves the conjecture. That is before the window, and I found no written argument behind it: no arXiv preprint by Oeding or Speck appears in the arXiv records, and the only later written item is the dissertation, whose abstract describes a reduction rather than a proof. The 2024 dissertation is the one in-window item that could contain the argument, and I could not read its text. Shitov's 2025 result is a genuine journal-refereed partial result (at most three non-real eigenvalues, all in B, with A real). The 2025 MDPI survey calls the problem open, and I could not check whether it mentions Speck or Oeding. The 2026 Mulero-Martinez paper may or may not concern this conjecture; its abstract was not read. Close calls: (a) whether the 2023 talk counts as a first written argument, since its date rests on an abstract and the rule dates a talk to its write-up, which I could not find; (b) whether the dissertation proves anything, which the abstract does not say and I could not verify; (c) whether Shitov's restriction makes it partial or a near-complete case; I read it as partial because the two excluded classes are large. AI: I searched for AI involvement with this conjecture by name and with terms for ChatGPT, GPT, Gemini, Claude, AlphaEvolve, Deep Think and formal verification. I found no source that names an AI system for this conjecture. The AI-tagged 2026 items I saw are about other problems (the Jacobian conjecture, an Erdos unit-distance result, and the determinant approximation conjecture, arXiv 2609.15567, whose abstract page I opened and which concerns Fuglede-Kadison determinants on group rings with no AI attribution on that page). The Google DeepMind formal-conjectures repository's top level has no Marcus or determinant entry, but I could not search its code, so the Lean status is unverified.
competing_reading: The strongest case for reading this as in-window progress: the 2024 dissertation was written after the 2023 claim, has the same advisor and co-author, and may contain the full argument. The abstract is written in the vocabulary of a proof strategy (a reduction to non-negative solutions of a rank-deficient system, plus modifications), and the 2023 abstract claims the complete geometric description proves the conjecture. If the dissertation body contains that proof, the status would be a claimed full proof from an embargoed PhD thesis, unreviewed and in-window. The opposite reading, which the record currently supports better: the dissertation abstract does not claim a proof, the 2024 talk claims only n=3, and the 2025 survey and 2025 Shitov paper treat the conjecture as open. On that reading nothing in the window settles the conjecture, and the 2023 claim is pre-window and unwritten.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of the Speck dissertation (etd.auburn.edu bitstream, 'Speck Dissertation Final.pdf'): whether it contains a proof of the containment for all n, or only for n=3 or a reduction, and whether any theorem is stated as settling the conjecture. (2) Any arXiv or journal version by Speck and/or Oeding, and its date. (3) The full text of the 2025 Bebiano-da Providencia survey (MDPI), in particular whether it cites or discusses the Speck-Oeding claim and what it lists as the state of the n=3 and general cases. (4) The Auburn seminar pages for 2023/01, 2024/01 and 2024/04 (currently redirect), to confirm the dates and abstracts of the Jan 2024 talk and the defense. (5) The abstract of Mulero-Martinez (LAA 740, 2026) to see whether it treats the containment. (6) A search of the google-deepmind formal-conjectures repository (FormalConjectures/) for a Marcus or determinant entry and its sorry status.
